description: The shared preset's contents are INLINED rather than extended via
github>brujack/ai-config//renovate-presets/default.json. ai-config is a PRIVATE repo, and a
repo that cannot read it throws config-validation at initRepo -- BEFORE any dependency
extraction -- so Renovate abandons the whole repository. No PRs, no dependency dashboard, no
signal of any kind. dotfiles is public and was therefore never once processed between its
renovate.json landing on 2026-05-18 and the inlining fix. CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-08-24: Renovate
ran here and raised #240 (pinned all six actions/checkout refs, auto-merged) and #241 (v7 major,
correctly held by the automerge:false major rule). mode=silent is no longer in force here.
Measured 2026-08-22 across the five repos configured before Renovate's only run (2026-06-06):
the two PRIVATE repos got 1 and 5 PRs; the three PUBLIC ones got zero. Perfect separation.
terraform_ansible's PR was titled 'update all non-major dependencies' -- this preset's own
groupName -- so the private repos demonstrably resolved it.
ai-config/renovate-presets/default.json remains the canonical text; keep the extends,
schedule, labels and packageRules keys below in sync with it. Nothing detects drift between
the copies -- see the backlog row.
pip_requirements is DELIBERATELY absent. Renovate's pattern for that manager is
(^|/)[\w-]*requirements([-._]\w+)?\.(txt|pip)$, which allows AT MOST ONE [-._]\w+ group after
'requirements', and \w excludes '-'. Measured against all five renderings: only
requirements-ci.txt matches. The four narrow slices are two-segment names and cannot -- which
is LUCK, not design, so a test pins it. All five are GENERATED from uv.lock; Renovate would
raise PRs against generated files that check-requirements-ci fails and the next
`make sync-requirements-ci` reverts. The declaration is pyproject.toml.
pinDigests implements ADR-0006. Was 0 of 6 refs pinned, all actions/checkout@v6; #240 made it
6 of 6 on Renovate's first real run here. It pins currently-unpinned refs rather than only preventing new drift, which is what made that a one-PR fix rather than a review obligation.
npm manages one dependency, json2yaml, which no lib/, scripts/ or Makefile line invokes --
enabled so the dead dependency surfaces as a PR rather than rotting silently.
